memory_candidates.content: When waiting on a unit started via 'systemctl --user start <unit>', poll completion with 'systemctl --user show <unit> -p ActiveState --value' and loop while the value is 'activating' or 'active'. 'systemctl --user is-active --quiet <unit>' only matches ActiveState==active and silently returns a false 'done' almost immediately for any Type=oneshot unit, because such a unit reports ActiveState=activating/SubState=start for its entire run and never transitions through 'active' at all.

A plan measuring something that requires calendar-spaced real-world observation (e.g. a drain rate across 5+ hand-run passes spanning a week) can be structured as one implementation phase per pass, each gated on '>=N hours since the previous pass's recorded timestamp'. Each dispatch legitimately advances at most one such phase and returns status partial with a stated next-eligible-time, rather than forcing multiple passes in one sitting (which would collapse the spacing the measurement itself depends on).

sapience_notes.subject: sapience-sync.service ActiveState during a run
sapience_notes.value: The Type=oneshot systemd unit sapience-sync.service holds ActiveState=activating/SubState=start for its entire run and never reports ActiveState=active. Polling with 'systemctl --user is-active --quiet' (which only matches ActiveState==active) returns a false-positive 'done' almost immediately; the correct predicate is 'systemctl --user show sapience-sync.service -p ActiveState --value', looping while the value is 'activating' or 'active'.

sapience_notes.subject: Sapience Pass 2 drain rate (2026-11-17)
sapience_notes.value: A 50-chunk sapience-sync pass that staged 539 objects left 'would ingest now' unchanged (118 before and after) because new transcripts accrued during the 22.5-minute run at a rate that offset the pass's consumption; 'Available on disk' grew +6 in the same window. A single pass's before/after delta on 'would ingest now' alone is not a reliable drain-rate proxy without separately accounting for concurrent accrual.

sapience_notes.subject: Sapience per-pass cost signal
sapience_notes.value: Neither 'sapience stats', the sapience-sync systemd journal, nor any file under ~/.sapience/ exposes a per-run token or dollar-cost counter for the anthropic backend -- only cumulative lifetime counts via 'sapience stats'. Independently confirmed on two separate passes (2026-11-13 and 2026-11-17).

sapience_notes.subject: Sapience extract-error partial-failure mode
sapience_notes.value: A sapience-sync pass can partially fail without the all-or-nothing pattern of the earlier ollama-402 outage: Pass 2 (2026-11-17) logged 34 extract error: lines (30 DNS 'Name or service not known', 3 read timeouts, 1 SSL handshake timeout) clustered in its final ~2 minutes -- a transient network outage -- yet still staged 539 of its 50-chunk batch. Any non-zero extract-error count still disqualifies that pass from a clean drain-rate computation even when most of the batch succeeded.

sapience_notes.subject: Task 136 measurement series pacing
sapience_notes.value: Task 136's plan structures its required 5+ pass measurement series as one implementation phase per calendar-spaced pass, each gated on at least 24 hours since the prior pass's recorded ledger timestamp. A single dispatch can therefore complete at most one new pass phase regardless of available work capacity; this is the plan's designed pacing and should be returned as status partial with the next-eligible-time stated, not forced early or treated as a blocker.

sapience_notes.subject: Sapience redaction-line absence convention
sapience_notes.value: The sapience-sync journal line 'Redacted N secret/PII value(s)' is only emitted when N>0 for that run; a run with zero redactions (Pass 2, 2026-11-17) emits no redaction line at all rather than an explicit 'Redacted 0' line, so its absence in a run's journal must be read as zero redactions, not as a missing-data gap.
